result.topic_en: Expansion of a quadratic line element $dx^2+dy^2+da^2+db^2$ in terms of partial derivatives, together with Cauchy–Riemann-type relations between derivatives of functions u and v of x, y, a, b, plus several geometric sketches (triangles, a hexagram, a parallelogram, solids).
result.transcription:
$dx^2+dy^2+da^2+db^2=ds^2=dx^2\left(\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}\right)^2 ...\right)+2\,dx\,dy\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}+...\right)$ [?]
$+2\,dx\,dy\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}+2\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}\right)$ [?]
$+dy^2\left(\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}\right)^2 ...\right)$ [?]
$+2\,da\,db\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}\frac{\partial x}{\partial ...}+...\right)$ [?]
$+2\,dd$ [?]

$\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}dx+\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}dy+\frac{\partial v}{\partial a}da+\frac{\partial v}{\partial b}db$

[-$\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}\quad\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\partial$-]
$\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}\qquad\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}$

$\frac{du+dvi}{dx}=\frac{du+dvi}{dy\,i}$

$-\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}dx+\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}dy-\frac{\partial u}{\partial b}da+\frac{\partial u}{\partial a}db$

$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y\partial a}-\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial b\partial x}=0$
